content_units: You have a realistic path into   Revenue Operations within 8 months   because your current background already overlaps with core RevOps work:   CRM hygiene/admin, forecasting, reporting, and cross-functional coordination  . The most realistic route is to target roles that sit between Sales Ops and full RevOps leadership, rather than aiming first for senior RevOps manager roles.
- Current strength match:   Sales Ops → RevOps Analyst / GTM Operations / Revenue Operations Specialist
- Most important gaps to close:   SQL, workflow automation, process design across sales-marketing-CS
- Compensation target:   EUR 70,000+ is realistic  , but easiest to reach through:
- roles emphasizing CRM, forecasting, BI, and cross-functional ops
- “A   B2B Sales Operations professional expanding into full-funnel Revenue Operations  ”
- Not as a beginner changing careers
- Not as a pure CRM admin
Role   Fit for your background   Likelihood in 8 months   Typical compensation fit   What gets you hired
Revenue Operations Analyst   Strong   High   Medium-High   SQL basics, funnel reporting, process thinking
Revenue Operations Specialist   Very Strong   High   High   CRM ownership, forecasting, dashboards, stakeholder alignment
GTM Operations Analyst   Strong   High   Medium-High   Cross-functional reporting, pipeline insights, systems support
Sales Operations Manager   Very Strong   High   High   Forecasting, governance, reporting leadership
Commercial Operations Analyst   Strong   Medium-High   Medium   Broader business ops exposure, BI reporting
Revenue Operations Manager   Partial stretch   Medium   High   Need stronger automation, SQL, and end-to-end RevOps stories
Best path for your target salary and timeline:
4.   Sales Operations Manager   at companies where Sales Ops feeds into RevOps
- Senior RevOps Manager roles requiring deep ownership of   marketing ops + CS ops + advanced architecture
- Technical operations roles heavily centered on   data engineering  , advanced SQL, or warehouse tooling
- Pure admin roles that cap compensation below your target
Skill Gaps That Matter Most First
Option 1:   SQL for RevOps     Learn SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, CASE, window basics; enough to query funnel and pipeline data   Highest priority
Option 2:   Automation workflows     Learn HubSpot workflows, Salesforce Flow basics, Zapier/Make logic, lead-routing and handoff automation   Directly marketable
Option 3:   RevOps funnel design     Understand lifecycle stages, attribution basics, pipeline definitions, SLA design, handoffs across marketing-sales-CS   Critical for interviews
Option 4:   BI storytelling     Move from dashboard building to executive-ready KPI narratives: conversion, pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, velocity   Strong interview differentiator
- Customer lifecycle metrics: churn, expansion, NRR, GRR
- Basic systems architecture: CRM + MAP + CS platform + BI stack
Certifications and Portfolio Work Worth Doing
Choose   2, not 6  . Hiring teams care more about role relevance than certificate volume.
Option 1:   HubSpot Revenue Operations Certification     Best signaling for RevOps fundamentals and funnel alignment   Relevant for transition story
Option 2:   Salesforce Administrator   or focused Salesforce Trailhead badges   Strong if Amsterdam target companies use Salesforce   Valuable if your CRM background includes Salesforce
Option 3:   SQL certificate/course completion     Useful only if paired with portfolio outputs   Better as proof-of-skill than prestige
Portfolio projects that are better than extra certifications
Build   3 compact portfolio case studies   and publish them on Notion or Google Drive as clean one-pagers/PDFs.
Option 1:   Pipeline & Forecast Accuracy Review     Show how you would improve stage definitions, forecast categories, and reporting cadence   Speaks directly to your background
Option 2:   Lead-to-Opportunity Funnel Redesign     Map lifecycle stages, conversion points, SLA handoffs, and 3 automation opportunities   Shows RevOps mindset
Option 3:   CRM Data Quality Dashboard     Create a dashboard for duplicates, missing fields, stale opportunities, and activity compliance   Highly credible and practical
Month 1-2   Build RevOps foundation   Learn SQL basics; map RevOps metrics; audit target job descriptions   Skills gap tracker + keyword bank
Month 3-4   Create marketable proof   Complete 2 portfolio case studies; start automation practice; refine LinkedIn/CV   Portfolio v1 + updated profile
Month 5-6   Start targeted outreach   Apply to selected firms; contact hiring managers/recruiters; do mock interviews   Interview pipeline
Month 7   Close remaining gaps   Add 1 certification; improve interview stories; build final case study   Portfolio v2 + stronger narratives
Month 8   Convert interviews to offers   Negotiate comp; target firms with international GTM teams; prioritize best-fit roles   Offer-ready applications
Focused Job Search Strategy for Amsterdam
Prioritize employers where RevOps is established and paid well:
- fintech, martech, HR tech, logistics tech
- US/UK-headquartered firms with Amsterdam or Netherlands GTM hubs
Use these searches in LinkedIn and job boards:
Your headline should emphasize transition without sounding junior:
-   B2B Sales Operations Specialist transitioning into RevOps
-   CRM, Forecasting, Reporting, GTM Process Improvement
Focus every bullet on business outcomes:
- stakeholder alignment across sales, finance, and leadership
Use a   tight list of 40-60 companies  , not broad mass applications.
- identify RevOps leader, Sales Ops lead, or GTM recruiter
- send short message with 1 relevant proof point
- attach or link 1 portfolio case study
- coordinating across sales, finance, and leadership
- designing a cleaner handoff or governance process
For   EUR 70,000+  , strongest odds come from:
- Revenue Operations Specialist at strong SaaS firms
- Sales Operations Manager with analytics/process scope
- RevOps Analyst at larger international companies with bonus/equity
- Amsterdam-based firms hiring in English-first environments
If the base salary lands slightly below target, evaluate:
- title growth path to RevOps Manager in 12-18 months
Your most realistic winning strategy is:
- target   Revenue Operations Specialist   and   Revenue Operations Analyst   roles first
- keep   Sales Operations Manager   as a parallel track
- spend the first 3-4 months on   SQL + automation + 2 portfolio case studies
- apply only to firms where RevOps is already a recognized function
- position yourself as   “already doing part of RevOps, now expanding to full-funnel operations”
This is more realistic than trying to rebrand immediately into a senior RevOps manager.
